We compare homological and homotopical epimorphisms of associative algebras in monoidal $\infty$-categories. Assume that geometric realizations and pushouts of associative algebras exist and that tensoring preserves geometric realizations. Then every homological epimorphism is homotopical. If, in addition, the ambient category is additive and tensoring preserves finite coproducts, the converse holds. This extends the result of Chuang and Lazarev for dg-algebras. In the symmetric monoidal setting, we discuss consequences for centers and commutative refinements, as well as applications to derived analytic geometry.

1. Introduction Let f : A → B f:A\to B be a morphism of associative algebras in a monoidal ∞ \infty -category 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} . The canonical maps B ∗ A B ⟶ B , B ⊗ A B ⟶ B B\ast_{A}B\longrightarrow B,\qquad B\otimes_{A}B\longrightarrow B give rise to two notions of epimorphism. We call f f homotopical if the first map is an equivalence and homological if the second is an equivalence. Here ∗ A \ast_{A} denotes the pushout of associative algebras and ⊗ A \otimes_{A} the relative tensor product of modules. Chuang and Lazarev prove that these notions agree for unbounded dg-algebras [ 14 , Theorem 4.4] and ask whether this equivalence reflects a general categorical phenomenon [ 14 , Remark 4.2] . We show that the equivalence can fail for associative algebras in spaces, equipped with the cartesian monoidal structure (see Remark 4.4 ). Theorem 3.8 establishes the equivalence in additive monoidal ∞ \infty -categories, provided the relevant algebra pushouts and geometric realizations exist and tensoring preserves finite coproducts and geometric realizations. Our motivation comes from bornological algebra and analytic geometry. See [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 8 , 12 ] for the bornological approach to derived analytic geometry, and [ 7 , 8 , 10 , 11 , 13 , 19 , 20 ] for further developments. In derived analytic geometry, localizations are naturally expressed by a tensor idempotence condition B ​ ⊗ ^ A 𝕃 ​ B ≃ B . B\widehat{\otimes}_{A}^{\mathbb{L}}B\simeq B. This condition occurs, for instance, in the homological description of affinoid, dagger, and Stein localizations [ 3 , 4 , 8 , 12 , 13 ] . See Section 4 for a more detailed account. On the other hand, in the noncommutative geometric framework of [ 6 ] , localization is formulated intrinsically in the category of associative algebras through the condition B ∗ A B ≃ B . B\ast_{A}B\simeq B. The equivalence between the pushout and tensor conditions is a key input in that work. Extending this localization formalism from the algebraic to the analytic setting therefore requires understanding when the two conditions agree. Establishing this comparison in a general monoidal setting is the main goal of this paper. The paper is organized as follows. Section 2 collects the preliminaries on algebras, modules, central structures, square-zero extensions, and derivations. Section 3 proves our main theorem. The proof that homotopical epimorphisms are homological epimorphisms is inspired by Silver’s argument for ordinary rings [ 32 ] : we construct a relative derivation with values in B ⊗ A B B\otimes_{A}B and show that its triviality forces relative multiplication to be an equivalence. Section 4 discusses the cotangent complex, examples motivating the theorem, and geometric applications. Appendix A gives an alternative proof under the additional assumption that 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} is closed. Notation We follow the conventions for simplicial sets and ∞ \infty -categories established in [ 24 ] . Let Δ \Delta denote the simplex category, and let 𝐬𝐒𝐞𝐭 = Fun ⁡ ( Δ op , 𝐒𝐞𝐭 ) \mathbf{sSet}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathbf{Set}) denote the category of simplicial sets. For each n ≥ 0 n\geq 0 , we write Δ n \Delta^{n} for the standard n n -simplex and, for 0 ≤ i ≤ n 0\leq i\leq n , we denote by Λ i n ↪ Δ n \Lambda_{i}^{n}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n} the inclusion of the i i -th horn. A simplicial set 𝒳 ∙ {\mathcal{X}}_{\bullet} is an ∞ \infty -category , or equivalently a weak Kan complex , if every inner horn in 𝒳 ∙ {\mathcal{X}}_{\bullet} admits a filler, that is, if it has the right lifting property with respect to Λ i n ↪ Δ n \Lambda_{i}^{n}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n} whenever 0 < i < n 0<i<n ; see [ 24 , Definition 1.1.2.4] . Given two objects x , y ∈ 𝒳 0 x,y\in{\mathcal{X}}_{0} , we denote by Map 𝒳 ​ ( x , y ) {\rm Map\,}_{{\mathcal{X}}}(x,y) the corresponding mapping space, in the sense of [ 24 , Definition 1.2.2.1] . For an ∞ \infty -category 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} , we write X ∈ 𝒞 X\in{\mathcal{C}} to mean that X X is an object of 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} . We denote by 𝐂𝐚𝐭 \mathbf{Cat} the ∞ \infty -category of small ∞ \infty -categories. Finally, if two objects x , y ∈ 𝒞 x,y\in{\mathcal{C}} are equivalent, we write x ≃ y x\simeq y . An ∞ \infty -category is called additive if it has finite biproducts and its canonical commutative monoid structures on mapping spaces are group-like. In particular, subtraction of morphisms is defined coherently. Additivity of 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} does not by itself assert that a chosen tensor product preserves these biproducts; this compatibility will always be stated separately. All fibers, pullbacks, and mapping spaces below are understood in the ∞ \infty -categorical sense. Throughout this paper, we use cohomological conventions for complexes.

Definition 2.1: A monoidal ∞ \infty -category is a coCartesian fibration of ∞ \infty -operads p : 𝒞 ⊗ ⟶ Assoc ⊗ . p:{\mathcal{C}}^{\otimes}\longrightarrow\mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes}. Its underlying ∞ \infty -category 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} is the fiber over the unique color of Assoc ⊗ \mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes} . The operadic Segal condition identifies the fiber over ⟨ n ⟩ \langle n\rangle with 𝒞 n {\mathcal{C}}^{n} . CoCartesian transport along the ordered binary multiplication and the nullary operation determines the tensor product ⊗ : 𝒞 × 𝒞 → 𝒞 \otimes:{\mathcal{C}}\times{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}} and its unit 1 𝒞 1_{\mathcal{C}} (see [ 23 , §4.1.1] ). A symmetric monoidal ∞ \infty -category is a coCartesian fibration of ∞ \infty -operads 𝒞 sym ⊗ → 𝐅𝐢𝐧 ∗ {\mathcal{C}}^{\otimes}_{\mathrm{sym}}\to\mathbf{Fin}_{*} (see [ 23 , Definition 2.0.0.7] ). It determines a monoidal ∞ \infty -category by the pullback 𝒞 ⊗ = Assoc ⊗ × 𝐅𝐢𝐧 ∗ 𝒞 sym ⊗ . {\mathcal{C}}^{\otimes}=\mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes}\times_{\mathbf{Fin}_{*}}{\mathcal{C}}^{\otimes}_{\mathrm{sym}}.

Definition 2.2: For a monoidal ∞ \infty -category p : 𝒞 ⊗ → Assoc ⊗ p:{\mathcal{C}}^{\otimes}\to\mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes} , define 𝐀𝐥𝐠 ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) = Fun / Assoc ⊗ inert ⁡ ( Assoc ⊗ , 𝒞 ⊗ ) , \mathbf{Alg}({\mathcal{C}})=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/\mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes}}(\mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}}^{\otimes}), the full subcategory of the functor ∞ \infty -category over Assoc ⊗ \mathrm{Assoc}^{\otimes} spanned by functors preserving inert morphisms. Thus its objects are inert-preserving sections of p p , called associative algebra objects in 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} .

Example 2.3: For a commutative dg-algebra A A over a commutative ring k k , let 𝐌𝐨𝐝 A \mathbf{Mod}_{A} denote the derived ∞ \infty -category of dg A A -modules, obtained by inverting quasi-isomorphisms and equipped with the derived tensor product. Then 𝐀𝐥𝐠 ⁡ ( 𝐌𝐨𝐝 A ) \mathbf{Alg}(\mathbf{Mod}_{A}) is modeled by associative dg A A -algebras with quasi-isomorphisms inverted. If 𝐒𝐩 \mathbf{Sp} denotes spectra with the smash product, 𝐀𝐥𝐠 ⁡ ( 𝐒𝐩 ) \mathbf{Alg}(\mathbf{Sp}) is the ∞ \infty -category of associative ring spectra.

Lemma 2.4: Let ( 𝒞 , ⊗ ) ({\mathcal{C}},\otimes) be a monoidal ∞ \infty -category with countable coproducts, and assume that ⊗ \otimes preserves countable coproducts in each variable. Then the forgetful functor 𝐀𝐥𝐠 ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) → 𝒞 \mathbf{Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to{\mathcal{C}} admits a left adjoint, called the free algebra functor .

Definition 3.1: A morphism f : A → B f:A\to B in 𝐀𝐥𝐠 ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) \mathbf{Alg}({\mathcal{C}}) is said to be - a homotopical epimorphism if the canonical morphism B ∗ A B → B B\ast_{A}B\to B is an equivalence, - a homological epimorphism if the canonical morphism B ⊗ A B → B B\otimes_{A}B\to B is an equivalence of B B -bimodules.

Lemma 3.2: Let f : A → B f:A\to B be an associative algebra morphism, and suppose that the pushout B ∗ A B B\ast_{A}B exists.
